paper_title: DLP Dynamic Layerwise Pruning in Large Language Models
caption_used: Comparison of per-output and per-layer perplexity at different sparsity rates using a logarithmic scale. Both pruning configurations maintain comparable perplexity below 10^1 for sparsity rates up to 50%, after which values begin to diverge. At 60% sparsity, the Per-Output configuration reaches approximately 15 while Per-Layer remains near 10^1. The most pronounced separation occurs at 70%, where Per-Output perplexity climbs to roughly 50 while Per-Layer reaches approximately 25. At 80% sparsity, both configurations approach 10^3, with Per-Output exhibiting marginally higher perplexity than Per-Layer at this extreme.

model_annotations.Bulgarian: Тази стълбовидна диаграма илюстрира връзката между степента на разреждане (sparsity rate) и перплексността (perplexity) за два различни подхода на изрязване - Per-Output и Per-Layer. Хоризонталната ос показва степента на разреждане като процент, със стойности от 10% до 80% на равни интервали, със съответните етикети. Вертикалната ос представя перплексността в логаритмична скала от $10^1$ до $10^3$, също с равни интервали и съответните етикети. За всеки процент на разреждане са дадени по две стълби, съответно за Per-Output и Per-Layer, които са ясно разграничени чрез различни цветове според легендата горе вляво. При 10% разреждане перплексността и за двата подхода е под $10^1$. С увеличаването на степента на разреждане до 50%, перплексността остава под $10^1$ и за двата подхода, като стойностите са близки. При 60% разреждане, перплексността на Per-Output е около 15, докато тази на Per-Layer е близо до $10^1$. При 70% разреждане, перплексността на Per-Output достига около 50, а на Per-Layer е около 25. При 80% разреждане и двата подхода показват перплексност близка до $10^3$, като Per-Output е малко по-висока от Per-Layer.
model_annotations.Chinese: The graph presents a comparison of per-output and per-layer perplexity at various sparsity rates. The horizontal axis represents the sparsity rate, ranging from 10% to 80% in increments of 10%, with a linear scale. The vertical axis represents perplexity on a logarithmic scale, labeled from 10^1 to 10^3. Two categories of bars are displayed: Per-Output, shown in blue, and Per-Layer, shown in orange. At the lowest sparsity rate of 10%, both categories have similar perplexity values, just above 10^1, with Per-Output slightly higher. As the sparsity rate increases to 50%, perplexity remains relatively stable for both categories, staying below 10^1. At 60%, Per-Output perplexity is approximately 15, while Per-Layer is near 10^1. A notable divergence occurs at 70%, where Per-Output perplexity is around 50 and Per-Layer is about 25. By 80%, both categories approach 10^3, with Per-Output showing marginally higher perplexity. The bars are not specifically sorted, and no visual emphasis is applied to any category.
model_annotations.English: This bar chart compares the perplexity of two pruning configurations, Per-Output and Per-Layer, across various sparsity rates. The horizontal axis represents the sparsity rate, labeled in percentage increments from 10% to 80%, with no indicated scale type. The vertical axis represents perplexity, labeled with a logarithmic scale ranging from 10^1 to 10^3. The Per-Output configuration is represented by blue bars, and the Per-Layer configuration is represented by orange bars. The bars for each configuration are grouped at each sparsity rate. At 10% sparsity, both configurations have a perplexity value slightly above 10^1. As sparsity increases, perplexity remains relatively stable up to 50%, with both configurations near 10^1. At 60% sparsity, the Per-Output bar reaches approximately 15, while the Per-Layer bar is near 10^1. The bars grow in height, with the Per-Output bar at 70% sparsity reaching roughly 50 and the Per-Layer bar reaching approximately 25. At 80% sparsity, both bars approach 10^3, with the Per-Output bar marginally higher than the Per-Layer bar. The bars are not sorted in any specific order beyond the increasing sparsity rate, and no bars are visually emphasized beyond their color-coded representation.
model_annotations.German: Das Diagramm zeigt einen Vergleich der Perplexity-Werte für zwei verschiedene Konfigurationen, Per-Output und Per-Layer, bei verschiedenen Sparsity-Raten. Die horizontale Achse stellt die Sparsity-Rate in Prozent dar, die Kategorien sind in gleichmäßigen Schritten von 10% angeordnet und reichen von 10% bis 80%. Die vertikale Achse repräsentiert die Perplexity auf einer logarithmischen Skala, mit einer Beschriftung und einem Wertebereich von etwa $10^0$ bis $10^3$, die Skala ist logarithmisch mit regelmäßigen Markierungen bei jedem Vielfachen von $10^1$. Die Balken sind in zwei Farben dargestellt: blau für Per-Output und orange für Per-Layer. Die niedrigsten Werte für beide Konfigurationen liegen bei einer Sparsity-Rate von 10%, wo Per-Output ungefähr bei 4 und Per-Layer bei 5 liegt. Die höchsten Werte werden bei einer Sparsity-Rate von 80% erreicht, wo Per-Output etwa bei 700 und Per-Layer bei 600 liegt. Die Balken sind in der Reihenfolge der zunehmenden Sparsity-Rate angeordnet und es gibt keine Hervorhebung einzelner Balken. Die Werte für beide Konfigurationen bleiben bis zu einer Sparsity-Rate von 50% unter $10^1$, danach beginnen sie zu divergieren.
